chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya and someone else, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Musa ibn Umar, from Ibn Sinan, from Abu Sa'id al-Qammat, from Bukayr ibn A'yan who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): For what reason did Allah place the Stone in the corner in which it is found, and not in any other corner? And for what reason is it kissed? And for what reason was it brought out from Paradise? And for what reason was the covenant of the servants and the pledge placed in it and not in any other? And what is the explanation for that? Inform me — may Allah make me your ransom — for my contemplation of this matter is truly astonishing.

He said: So he (the Imam) said: You have asked and complicated yourself with the question, and investigated thoroughly. So understand the answer, free your heart, and direct your hearing. I shall inform you, if Allah wills. Allah, Blessed and Exalted, placed the Black Stone — which is a jewel that was brought out from Paradise to Adam (peace be upon him) — in that corner due to the reason of the covenant. And that is because when He took from the offspring of Adam, from their backs, their progeny, at the time when Allah took the covenant upon them in that place, and in that place He manifested Himself to them. And from that place the bird shall descend upon al-Qa'im (peace be upon him).

The first to pledge allegiance to him shall be that bird, which is, by Allah, Jibra'il (peace be upon him). And al-Qa'im shall lean his back against that station. It is the proof and the evidence upon al-Qa'im, and it is a witness for whoever was loyal to it in that place, and the witness against whoever fulfilled the covenant and pledge to it which Allah, Mighty and Majestic, took upon the servants.

As for the kissing and the istilam (touching), it is due to the reason of the covenant — a renewal of that covenant and primordial pledge, and a renewal of the pledge of allegiance — so that they fulfill to it the covenant which Allah took from them in the primordial pledge, and so that they come to it every year and fulfill to it that covenant and trust which were taken from them. Do you not see that you say: 'My trust I have fulfilled, and my pledge I have renewed' — so that it may witness for you regarding fulfillment?

By Allah, none fulfills that except our Shi'a, and none has preserved that covenant and primordial pledge except our Shi'a. And indeed they come to it and it recognizes them and confirms them, while others come to it and it repudiates them and belies them — and that is because none has preserved that except you.

For you, by Allah, it witnesses, and against them, by Allah, it witnesses — of betrayal and denial and disbelief. And it is the conclusive proof from Allah against them on the Day of Resurrection: it will come possessing a speaking tongue and two eyes in its original form, recognized by all creation without denial. It witnesses for whoever fulfills his appointment with it and renews the covenant and the primordial pledge with it — regarding the preservation of the covenant and the pledge and the fulfillment of the trust — and it witnesses against every one who denied and repudiated and forgot the primordial pledge, of disbelief and denial.

As for the reason why Allah sent it out from Paradise — do you know what the Stone was? I said: No. He said: It was an angel from among the great angels near Allah. When Allah took from the angels the primordial pledge, that angel was the first to believe in it and affirm it. So Allah took him as a trustee over all of His creation, deposited into him the primordial pledge and entrusted him with it, and obligated creation to renew with him every year the affirmation of the primordial pledge and covenant which Allah the Mighty and Majestic took from them.

Then Allah placed him with Adam in Paradise, reminding him of the primordial pledge and renewing the affirmation with him every year. Then when Adam disobeyed and was expelled from Paradise, Allah caused him to forget the covenant and the primordial pledge which He had taken from him and from his children — for Muhammad, may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace, and for his designated successor, peace be upon him — and He made him wandering and bewildered.

Then when Allah accepted Adam's repentance, He transformed that angel into the form of a white pearl and cast it from Paradise to Adam, peace be upon him, while he was in the land of India. When Adam looked at it he felt companionship with it, though he did not recognize it as more than a gemstone. Then Allah the Mighty and Majestic made it speak, and it said to him: 'O Adam, do you recognize me?' He said: 'No.' It said: 'Indeed! Satan has overpowered you and caused you to forget the remembrance of your Lord.'

Then it transformed into the form in which it had been with Adam in Paradise, and said to Adam: 'Where is the covenant and the primordial pledge?' Adam leapt towards it, remembered the primordial pledge, wept, humbled himself before it, kissed it, and renewed the affirmation of the covenant and the primordial pledge. Then Allah the Mighty and Majestic transformed it into the gemstone of the Black Stone — a white, pure, radiating pearl.

Adam, peace be upon him, carried it on his shoulder in reverence and glorification. Whenever he became tired, Jibra'il, peace be upon him, carried it for him until he arrived with it at Mecca. He continually found companionship with it in Mecca and renewed the affirmation with it every day and night. Then indeed when Allah the Mighty and Majestic built the Ka'ba, He placed the Stone in that place — because when He, the Blessed and Most High, took the primordial pledge from the children of Adam, He took it in that place, and in that place He deposited the primordial pledge into the angel. And for that reason it was placed in that corner.

And He moved Adam from the place of the House to al-Safa, and Eve to al-Marwa, and placed the Stone in that corner. Then when Adam looked from al-Safa and the Stone had already been placed in the corner, he proclaimed 'Allahu Akbar', declared 'La ilaha illa Allah', and glorified Him. Therefore the tradition was established of the Takbir and facing the corner in which the Stone is, from al-Safa.

For indeed Allah entrusted him with the primordial pledge and the covenant instead of others from the angels, because when Allah the Mighty and Majestic took the primordial pledge for Himself of Lordship, and for Muhammad — may Allah bless him and his family — of Prophethood, and for Ali, peace be upon him, of succession/guardianship, the sides of the angels trembled. And the first one who hastened to affirm was that angel — there was none among them more intense in love for Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, may Allah bless him and his family, than him. And for that reason Allah chose him from among them and deposited into him the primordial pledge. And it will come on the Day of Resurrection possessing a speaking tongue and a seeing eye, witnessing for every one who fulfilled his appointment to that place and preserved the primordial pledge.

ai.seo_question: Why is the Black Stone placed in the corner of the Ka'ba and why is it kissed in Islam?
ai.summary: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS) explains to Bukayr ibn A'yan the mystical and cosmic significance of the Black Stone (al-Hajr al-Aswad). The Stone was originally an angel — the greatest believer among the angels when the primordial covenant (mithaq) was taken — who was transformed into a jewel and entrusted with the covenant of all humanity. The Imam reveals that the kissing and touching of the Stone during Hajj is a ritual renewal of the primordial covenant that all souls made with Allah before creation, and that the Stone will bear witness on the Day of Judgment for those who honored the covenant (the Shia) and against those who broke it.
